rounds.proof_sketch: For float32 (main contract): mutated selu_kernel_optimized is never called; selu_kernel_float32 is used instead. For float16 (dtype stress): size=262144, threads=32768, each thread processes 8 elements. Extra iteration (i=8) writes to idx+8, which is the same index the next thread writes with i=0. Both compute identical SELU values. Last thread's extra iteration is blocked by bounds check (262144 < 262144 = false).
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the loop from 8 to 9 iterations in selu_kernel_optimized, but this kernel is only used for float16 inputs (not the main float32 contract). When executed with float16, the extra iteration either writes a duplicate value to an index that will be written identically by the next thread, or is blocked by the bounds check for the last thread. Since SELU is a deterministic point-wise function, redundant writes of the same computed value produce identical results. The mutation cannot be distinguished from the original by any input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The mutation affects a kernel (selu_kernel_optimized) that is not used for float32 inputs. For float16 inputs where it IS used, the extra loop iteration is semantically equivalent due to deterministic overlapping writes and bounds checking.
rounds.recommendations: This mutation reveals a coverage gap in mutation testing: mutations in dtype-specific code paths may not be exercisable under fixed-dtype contracts. Consider: (1) designing dtype as a configurable parameter in the testing contract, (2) adding explicit dispatch coverage metrics to ensure all kernel variants are tested with their intended types, (3) using static analysis to identify dead code paths under fixed input specifications.
